arguments.task: Review a core patch that moves image source resolving from Extbase ImageService into ResourceFactory and switches image ViewHelpers to it
arguments.area: core Resource / extbase Service / fluid ViewHelpers

arguments.query: breaking change what a patch owes
changelog entry file naming and content

arguments.message:
[TASK] Resolve file sources in ResourceFactory

Turning a loosely typed image source - as supplied by a Fluid
template - into a File or FileReference lived in Extbase's
ImageService, even though nothing about it is Extbase specific.

ResourceFactory->resolveFileObject() takes over: it passes through
File and FileReference, unwraps domain objects via
getOriginalResource(), and resolves UIDs, combined identifiers,
"EXT:" paths, legacy storage-0 paths and "t3://file" URNs. In
contrast to retrieveFileOrFolderObject() it never returns a folder
and throws instead of returning null, which is what the callers
need.

"t3://file" is link syntax, so the LinkService is now injected into
the ResourceFactory to resolve it. This does not introduce a
circular service dependency: LinkService only requires an event
dispatcher, and none of the registered link handlers declares a
constructor. Note that a third party link handler injecting the
ResourceFactory would recurse.

f:image, f:uri.image and the backend ThumbnailViewHelper use the
factory directly now, so no image ViewHelper depends on
ImageService anymore. ImageService->getImage() delegates and the
service is down to a single constructor argument.

The backend "../" prefix stripping is dropped along the way. It
compensated for links relative to the /typo3/ directory, which
does not exist since v13.

Resolves: #110359
Releases: main
Change-Id: Id53f1068d3866128320487df9ec59530d94a4aa1

outcomes.evidence: The skill is the session's first call, `references/base.md` and `references/checklist.md` are calls 2 and 3, and `typo3_project_scope` follows before any file of the checkout is opened. The patch is established at calls 7 to 9 — `git status --porcelain=v1` with the branch, `git log -1 --format=full` with `git show --stat`, and a reading of the two working-tree entries — and the hunks of all seven files at calls 13 and 14, ahead of the two `typo3_rule_lookup` calls that select what the patch owes. That is tighter than the run before it, where the rules were asked before the hunks were read. Every lookup takes an argument out of that one reading: `typo3_forge_lookup` the `Resolves:` number, `typo3_gerrit_lookup` the `Change-Id`, `typo3_task_guide` and `typo3_test_run_guide` the changed paths, `typo3_commit_message_guide` the message verbatim. Nearby tests are established rather than assumed, and the subsystem is followed where the patch points — into `PathUtility::getCanonicalPath()`, `LinkService::__construct()`, the seven registered link handlers and the three ViewHelpers' catch blocks.

Nine findings, every one with a path and a line, each tied to a rule or a traced behaviour and a consequence, and every one attributed. The blocking finding is the model: `ResourceFactory.php:206-220` drops the backend `../` strip, and rather than asserting a consequence the run traces it — `PathUtility::getCanonicalPath()` removes a leading `..` only in the `elseif ($absolutePathPrefix)` branch, so on a relative path it stays, `is_file()` and `is_dir()` both miss, `resolveFileObject()` throws 1625585158, and each ViewHelper catches it and re-throws as a Fluid `Exception`. It then refutes the commit message's own justification: `Deprecation-87889` deprecated the entry point script and says "It is still in place in case webserver configuration has not been adapted yet", and `entryPoint` is still `/typo3`. Three of those were re-checked against the checkout while judging and all three hold verbatim, including the `elseif` that decides the trace. The rule is quoted from the contribution rules — a change that moves or removes core functionality third-party code may use is `Breaking` — so the finding lands as a missing `[!!!]` and a missing `Breaking-110359-*.rst` rather than as an opinion about severity. The run before this one, on the same patch, reported no blocker at all and carried the opposite claim about those catch blocks.

The first half holds and the second is absent for the third recorded run in a row. Narrowest first: functional against `ResourceFactoryTest` alone, functional against the three image ViewHelper test classes, `unit` against a single `ImageScriptServiceTest`, then `cgl -n` and `phpstan` over the tree, all five through `CI=true ./Build/Scripts/runTests.sh` with what each printed quoted. Nothing anywhere in the answer is labelled available and not run: a search for that shape returns nothing on `not run`, `available`, `unrun` or `acceptance`, while `typo3_test_run_guide` was called with the changed paths and returned more than the five that ran. What makes this the third instance rather than a repeat is that the skill already states the rule in as many words — "Anything it did not run stays labelled as available rather than passing" — in the section the run demonstrably followed for everything else in it. The instruction is present, delivered and ignored, which is a question about the wording rather than about a missing rule.

All five are raised and each is anchored in this diff. Public API: the added public `resolveFileObject()` against the `Feature` rule, with `Important-107735` (14.0) as the precedent in the same class, and the constructor argument `ResourceFactory` gained. Compatibility: the `../` removal traced to its exception, and `main` / 15.0-dev checked against both the Gerrit branch and the issue's target version. Changelog: judged rather than demanded, and argued across the series — part 1 shipped no entry either, but part 1 added no public API and removed no behaviour. Commit shape: the guide reports no readiness issue and the answer says what the guide does not check, which is the `[!!!]` question. Review readiness is answered from the issue itself: Forge #110359 has an empty description, so the patch has to be understood from the message alone. Nothing is raised that the diff does not carry.

The order is argued and the boundaries are stated. Findings run blocks submission, sent back, worth changing, correct and checked, dropped while reading, and finding #3 is explicitly bounded — "genuinely arguable, so treat it as a reviewer will ask, not as settled". The `null` and scalar-`image` findings are each closed with why core cannot reach them and named as a line for the commit message rather than a code change. Nothing was rewritten and nothing was written at all: no `Write` call was made anywhere in the session, the answer stands in the response, and `git status` in the checkout after the run is the `M .gitignore` and `?? opencode.json` that `todo/reference/` records as this environment's standing state. It closes by naming `typo3-core-patch-development` as the owner of the work and the list as its work list.

failures.evidence: The diff is read before anything is asserted, and the reading goes past the diff wherever a finding needs it: `PathUtility` for what a leading `..` does, `DefaultConfiguration` for the backend entry point and the seven link handlers, the three ViewHelpers for what catches the exception. Where the commit message makes a claim, the claim is tested — the circular-dependency argument is confirmed by reading `LinkService` and every handler, and the `../` justification is refuted by reading the changelog entry it points at.

Two targeted `typo3_rule_lookup` queries and no contribution guide is emitted. The five suites that ran were chosen from what `typo3_test_run_guide` returned for the changed paths, and the narrowest names a single test file. What the answer does not do is name the ones it left, which is the third criterion rather than this failure mode.

The checkout is treated as core throughout: Gerrit trailers read as such, the change confirmed on the review server by its `Change-Id`, `Releases: main` against a branch one commit ahead of `origin/main`, the owed entries placed under `typo3/sysext/core/Documentation/Changelog/`, and every check run through `Build/Scripts/runTests.sh`. The working-tree finding is argued from the Gerrit workflow for this patch — `git commit --amend -a` would stage the `.gitignore` hunk into the patch set.

No file in the checkout changed, no commit was amended, nothing was pushed, and unlike the run before it no `Write` call was made at all. `git status` in `/home/benji/projects/typo3-cms` after the run is what it was before it.

notes:
The fourth recorded `REVIEW-03` run and the first that repeats a patch. Session `7110a716-71ed-424e-8ded-804df57377e3`, 2026-08-03 13:08-13:17 CEST, `claude-opus-5`, Claude Code 2.1.220, one prompt on standard input and no steering. 53 calls, 14 of them to this server. The run it replaces is in commit ca18f2b.

It is the comparison the run before it could not be. Same commit `9f6c6eb9093`, same working tree, same criteria digest, and the skill is what changed: `D-SKL-008` had added the two lookups and `D-SKL-007` the three dispositions, published into this checkout at 13:05 from server `8c01355`.

What the routing bought, in the run's own first paragraph. `typo3_forge_lookup` with the `Resolves:` number and `typo3_gerrit_lookup` with the `Change-Id` — the stable identifier rather than the change number, which is what the skill and the tool's own schema now ask for. Out of that: the issue is "Avoid calling ImageService methods - part 2", the change is 95070 at patch set 1 with no reviewer comments, part 1 is `0ba69a4a841` (#110355) and already merged, and the local commit and the pushed change carry the same `Change-Id` and subject — which is the check the skill states against a swapped number, performed and reported. The empty Forge description becomes a review-readiness finding. None of that was reachable in the run before, which closed by saying the issue had not been fetched.

The series reading then does work rather than sitting in the header. The changelog finding is argued against part 1 — it shipped no entry either, but it added no public API and removed no behaviour, so the precedent does not carry — which is the author's case made against the finding before it is reported.

Where the two runs disagree, this one is right. The run before reported no blocker and dismissed the exception path on the premise that the ViewHelpers catch only `ResourceDoesNotExistException`; that premise was false and its dismissal was caught by being written down. This run traces the same path to the `elseif ($absolutePathPrefix)` in `PathUtility::getCanonicalPath()`, names the three catch blocks correctly, refutes the commit message's justification against `Deprecation-87889` and the still-current `/typo3` entry point, and lands the finding as a missing `[!!!]` with a missing `Breaking` entry. Three of its readings were re-checked against the checkout while judging and all three hold verbatim.

The surface table moved too. Nine bare `assessed` rows became ten rows that each carry what the verdict rests on, the security row inline — "path resolution is touched, but the diff only narrows what resolves and adds no new sink or caller" — which is what `R-SKL-013` asks for. No row is `unassessed`, and the run covered all ten, so nothing here says whether the honest word would be used when it is owed.

What did not move is the third criterion, now unmet three runs running. The skill states the rule in the section this run otherwise followed exactly, and the run still reports five green suites with no line saying what `typo3_test_run_guide` returned beside them. Present, delivered, ignored: that is a question about the wording rather than about a missing rule, and it is the one thing worth taking out of this run.
